purpose: Test whether a designed reflection ritual creates clearer first value and a reason to return than a generic AI chat experience.
consentBoundary: Participation is voluntary and may stop at any time.
Do not ask participants to share birth data, private chats, journal entries, photos or health details.
Do not pay for positive feedback, app opens or referrals.
Store only an approved research summary after consent; do not place raw answers in the portable framework.
questions: What made the first invitation feel relevant or irrelevant to you?
What did you expect to happen after the first call to action?
Which wording felt distinct from a general AI chat tool, if any?
Which wording felt vague, over-promising or difficult to trust?
What would make a reflection ritual worth returning to on another day?
Where would you expect control, consent or an opt-out choice?
Which part of the first-use journey felt unclear?
What question would you want the product to help you explore without deciding for you?
What would make you stop using the experience after one try?
What should Nilaza prove before it asks you to join a beta?
analysisOutput: aggregate JTBD themes, objections, language snippets approved for internal synthesis, and product/content tickets without identifiers
